title: SLO-anchored KPI mapping & drift protocol (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working protocol for mapping customer-facing SLOs to concrete operational KPIs, defining metric calculations and cardinality rules, and specifying an automated drift detection + trace-capture workflow. Aim: reduce time-to-triage for SLO regressions and avoid noisy dashboards that hide signal behind cost.

Scope / audience:
- Observability owners, oncall SREs, serving runtime engineers, product owners for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Focused on inference request surface: token latency, token cost, model quality regressions, cache behavior, and routing fallbacks.

High-level SLO -> KPI mapping (examples):
1) SLO: request-success-rate (global) >= 99.95% monthly
   KPI metric: service.requests.success_rate (derived)
   Definition: 1 - (requests.failed / requests.total) aggregated per minute and rolled to 30d window
   Owner: eng-sre
   Cardinality: low (tenant, region, route)
   Alert: burn-rate exceed 2x for 30m or instantaneous drop > 0.2%

2) SLO: p99 tail latency for interactive endpoints <= 450ms
   KPI metric: inference.latency.p99_ms (per-model, per-route)
   Definition: 99th percentile of end-to-end request latency excluding prewarm/live migration windows; aggregation window 5m for alerting, 1h for dashboard smoothing
   Owner: eng-serving-runtime
   Cardinality: high for model_version, route, tenant (but see cardinality guidance below)
   Alert: p99 > 450ms for 5 consecutive 5m windows or p95 > 300ms and p99 rising > 30% baseline

3) SLO: unit-cost stability (monthly) +/- 10%
   KPI metric: billing.unit_cost_per_100k_tokens (hosted/dedicated)
   Definition: aggregated cost / total tokens * 100k; compare to rolling baseline last 30d
   Owner: finance/infra-calc

Metric definitions & instrumentation notes (recommended canonical names):
- inference.request.count: increment per request start (label: route, model, region, tenant_id, model_variant)
- inference.request.success{0,1}: tag success/failure
- inference.latency.ms: histogram (buckets tuned for 1ms..10s) with exemplars linked to trace id
- model.kv_cache.hit_ratio: gauge (numerator: cached_kv_reads, denom: total_kv_reads) per model_version, per shard
- batch.size.distribution: summary with p50/p90/p99 and raw bucket counts
- token.generated.count: cumulative counter
- pipeline.fallback.rate: rate of fallback-to-variant / total requests (label: reason=capacity|error|policy)

Cardinality guidance (practical rules):
- Keep cardinality small on high-cardinality metrics (request.count, latency): only include route/model_version/region. Avoid tenant_id on raw counters unless sampled.
- For tenant-level diagnostics create separate tenant-tracking metrics via downsampling or periodic per-tenant rollups (e.g., tenant.latency.p95_daily)
- Use label-value hashing for temporary experimental labels and prune after 7d

Trace capture & sampling policy (protocol):
- Anchors for trace linking (must be added to every request span): request_id, session_id (if present), tenant_id (hashed), model_version, route, shard_id
- Sampling tiers:
  * Tier 0 (always): traces for any request with status != 200 OR where model.kv_cache.hit_ratio < 0.2 OR pipeline.fallback.rate > 0.01 - always sample at 100%
  * Tier 1 (high-token): requests with token.generated.count > 200 - sample 10%
  * Tier 2 (statistical baseline): uniform sample 1% of requests for baseline drift detection
  * Emergency escalation: if any SLO breach detected (p99 breach or error-rate spike), flip to 100% sampling for affected route/model for 30 minutes automatically
- Exemplar policy: attach exemplar IDs to latency histogram buckets for tail requests (p99/p999) to speed root cause mapping from metric -> trace

Drift detection algorithm (initial prototype):
- Inputs: distribution of inference.latency.ms, batch.size.distribution, model.output.eval_metrics (synthetic tests), kv_cache.hit_ratio, token cost per request
- Compute daily KL-divergence of latency distribution between baseline-window (last 7d) and recent-window (24h). Thresholds: KL > 0.12 triggers medium alert; KL > 0.3 triggers investigation alert.
- Complement with change in synthetic eval pass rate (>= 2% drop) or increase in prompt-replay hallucination rate -> escalate to ML quality oncall
- Maintain a drift scoreboard per model_version with: KL_latency, delta_kv_hit, delta_p95, delta_cost_unit

Dashboard design notes (cost-aware):
- Top-level SLO panel: SLO gauges (error rate, p99 latency, unit-cost) with burn-rate sparkline and active incidents list
- Heatmap: latency heatmap per route x time (5m buckets) with tenant-cold-cache overlay toggle (shows cold_cache=true samples)
- Drilldowns: from any SLO widget link to time-bounded investigation view that auto-inserts query filters and trace anchors
- Cost panel: query-cost and ingestion-cost per dashboard widget; default dashboard load uses cached snapshot; live widgets have a cost warning badge
- Widget defaults: set query resolution to 5m, max lookback 7d for operational dashboards. Longer windows for retrospective only

Runbook excerpt (on p99 breach):
1) Open SLO panel, note affected route/model and start time
2) Check recent deploys (github:infra/serving-deploys and JIRA releases) -> if deploy within last 30m, tag as candidate
3) Check kv_cache.hit_ratio and cache-heatmap; if cold-cache event, mark and initiate warm-up synthetic calls
4) Pull exemplar traces for top 10 p99 requests -> look for repeated root cause (GC pause, large batch, external API stall)
5) If capacity/queueing observed, consider temporary scale-up or failover to model_variant (see pipeline.fallback.rate)
6) Create incident with initial hypothesis, link traces and dashboards, notify product owners

Query cost & telemetry budget rules:
- Each dashboard has an assigned query budget per 24h. Operational SLO dashboards get 200 queries/day; deep forensic dashboards 50 queries/day. Exceeding budget triggers reduction to cached snapshots only.
- Use downsampled materialized aggregates for p99 calculation where possible (pre-aggregated quantile sketches) to reduce cardinality and compute cost

Ownership and lifecycle:
- Metric owners must review metric usefulness quarterly. Stale metrics (>90d without panel usage) should be flagged for removal.
- New metrics need a feature flag and a short-lived 14d retention while we evaluate cardinality impact before making them permanent

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether tenant_id should ever be on raw latency histograms for Dedicated customers (privacy vs debuggability) -> owner: legal+privacy consult
- Define concrete KL thresholds per model class (smaller models have noisier latency profiles) -> action: collect baseline across top 20 models (JIRA:OBS-1147)
- Implement automated ephemeral trace store for emergency 24-72h retention to keep long traces out of long-term storage but available during incidents

Next steps (near term):
- Prototype drift scoreboard nightly job (owner: Luis) - target rollout to staging by 2026-03-01
- Add exemplars to latency histograms for p99 in the serving runtime (owner: Samira) - PR: github:infra/serving-prs#402
- Build dashboard templates with cost budgets and linkable trace anchors (owner: Jordan) - design doc: confluence:OBS-1572-dashboard-templates

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep cardinality: model_version, route, region. Tenant-level only via rollups.
- ALERT: emergency 100% trace on SLO breach is super useful but watch storage egress costs; add throttle by tenant for Hosted tier.
- Link to prompt-replay tooling from every quality dashboard (makes triage 3x faster).

References & links:
- Confluence: canonical SLO catalog (OBS-1423)
- GitHub: infra/observability-prs#238, infra/serving-prs#402
- Jira: OBS-982 (drift detection), OBS-1147 (KL thresholds research)

---
End of doc (working draft). Will iterate after feedback in slack:#observability and the Feb 2026 SLO sync.
